ko.title: [마케팅 101 #8] 당신의 $4.99 커피가 실은 커피에 관한 게 아닌 이유

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > 가격은 마케팅 중 유일하게 돈을 벌어들이는 요소이고, 나머지는 모두 돈을 쓴다. 이 강의에서는 가격이 어떻게 결정되는지, 왜 $9.99가 $10보다 저렴하게 느껴지는지, 그리고 같은 항공편의 같은 좌석이 세 가지 다른 가격으로 판매될 수 있는지를 다룬다.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람들은 가격 책정을 산술로 생각한다: 비용을 모두 더하고, 이윤을 얹고, 끝.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: 그것은 하나의 실제 방법이지만, 가장 흥미로운 방법은 아니다.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: 기업들이 가격을 정하는 세 가지 넓은 방법이 있다.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **원가 기반 가격 책정.** 물건을 만드는 데 드는 비용으로 시작해서, 마크업을 더한다.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: 재료비에 $4를 쓰고 70% 식재료 마진을 원하는 레스토랑은 약 $13에 도달한다.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: 간단하고 안전하지만, 한 가지 맹점이 있다: 당신의 비용은 고객의 관심사가 아니다.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: 누구도 그 요리를 $13에 원하지 않으면, 수학은 신경 쓰지 않는다.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **경쟁 기반 가격 책정.** 다른 사람들이 어떤 가격을 책정하는지 보고, 자신을 그에 대해 위치시킨다 — 일치, 약간 낮게, 또는 의도적으로 높게.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: 주유소는 거의 실시간으로 이렇게 한다.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: 위험은 당신의 전략을 경쟁자들에게 아웃소싱하는 것이고, 만약 그들이 틀리면 당신도 틀린다는 것이다.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **가치 기반 가격 책정.** 다른 쪽 끝에서 시작한다: 구매자에게 이것의 가치는 얼마인가?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: $200짜리 처방 안경과 $600짜리 안경은 만드는 데 거의 같은 비용이 들 수 있다.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: 그 차이는 구매자가 프레임에 대해 믿는 것이다.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 이것이 대부분의 마케터가 추구하는 방법인데, 스프레드시트 대신 고객으로부터 시작하기 때문이다.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: 그 다음은 두 번째 층이 있다: **심리적 가격 책정** — 그 숫자가 어떻게 읽히는지, 그것이 무엇인지만이 아니라.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *매력 가격 책정*: $10 대신 $9.99. 연구는 일반적으로 수요의 작지만 실제적인 상승을 보여주는데, 주로 우리가 좌에서 우로 읽고 "9"에 고정되기 때문이다. 효과는 미미하지만 가치 중심의 일상적인 구매에서 가장 잘 작동한다.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *프리미엄 가격 책정*: $499보다는 깔끔한 $500. 명품의 경우, 깔끔한 숫자는 신뢰를 나타낸다; 할인 신호는 제품을 훼손할 것이다.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *앵커링*: $1,200짜리 노트북을 $799짜리 옆에 보여주면 $799는 합리적으로 느껴진다. 당신이 보는 첫 번째 숫자가 정신적 기준을 설정한다.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *미끼 효과*: 작은 팝콘 $4, 큰 팝콘 $8은 무리가 있어 보인다 — $7.50의 중간 사이즈가 나타날 때까지. 그러면 큰 팝콘은 갑자기 저렴해 보인다. 중간 사이즈는 판매하기 위해 있는 것이 아니다; 큰 팝콘을 좋게 보이기 위해 있다.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: 세 번째 층: **가격 차등** — 기본적으로 같은 것에 대해 다른 구매자에게 다른 가격을 부과한다.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: 의심스러워 보이고, 이름도 도움이 되지 않지만, 대개는 합법적이고 종종 모두를 더 잘 살게 만든다.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: 경제학자들은 이를 세 가지 정도로 분류한다:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *1도 가격 차등*: 고객당 맞춤 가격. 소매에서는 드물고, 자동차 딜러십과 B2B 계약에서는 흔하다.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *2도 가격 차등*: 가격은 **당신이 선택한 것**에 따라 달라진다 — 크기, 등급, 또는 수량. Costco 대량 팩, Spotify Free vs. Premium, 커피숍의 12/16/20온스 컵. 고객들이 스스로 분류한다.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *3도 가격 차등*: 가격은 **당신이 누구인지**에 따라 달라진다 — 학생, 노인, 또는 군인 할인; 지역별 가격 책정.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: 통일하는 개념: 다른 사람들은 다른 금액을 지불할 의향이 있고, 단일 가격은 돈을 테이블에 남기거나 고객을 뒤에 남긴다.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: 가격 차등은 판매자가 양쪽 끝을 더 많이 포착하게 한다.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: 알아둘 가치가 있는 법적 주의: 미국에서는 다른 *소비자*에게 다른 가격을 부과하는 것이 일반적으로 괜찮다.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: Robinson-Patman 법은 같은 상품의 *경쟁하는 사업 구매자*들 간의 가격 차등을 제한하고, 독점금지법은 *가격 담합* — 경쟁자들이 가격에 동의하는 것을 금지한다.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: 그것들은 노인 할인과는 다른 것들이다.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: Chicago O'Hare에서 Denver로 가는 항공편을 예약하면, 한 화면에서 세 가지 층을 모두 볼 수 있다.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: 항공사는 비용으로 가격을 책정하지 않는다.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: 비행기가 날아가면, 한 명의 추가 승객의 한계 비용은 대략 그들의 체중 연료와 음료 캔이다 — $30이라고 하자.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: 그러나 같은 항공기에서 같은 화요일에 운임은 $89에서 $450까지 다양하다.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: 그것이 **가치 기반 가격 책정**이 **가격 차등**을 만나는 것이다.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: $450를 내는 사람은 누구인가?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: 월요일 아침에 예약하고, 목요일 밤에 돌아오는, 8일 전에 예약한 컨설턴트.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: $89를 내는 사람은 누구인가?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: 7주 전에 예약하고, 화요일부터 토요일까지 비행하고, 뒤쪽의 중간 좌석이 괜찮은 여행자.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: 항공사는 절대 "당신은 사업 여행자입니까?"라고 묻지 않는다.

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — 그럴 필요가 없다.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: 그것은 울타리를 만든다: 선구매 요구 사항, 토요일 밤 숙박, 변경 수수료.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: 사업 여행자들은 그 울타리를 뛰어넘지 않으므로, 비싼 운임으로 스스로 분류한다.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: 그것이 교과서적인 2도 가격 차등이다.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: 이제 좌석 지도를 보자.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: 기본 이코노미 $89, 메인 캐빈 $129, 컴포트+ $189.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: 대부분의 여행자들은 기본을 선택하지 않는다 — 기내 수하물이나 좌석 선택을 허용하지 않는다.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: 그것은 주로 $129를 합리적인 중간으로 느끼게 하기 위해 존재한다.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **미끼 효과**, 자연 상태에서.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: 그리고 운임은 $130이 아니라 $129로 읽힌다.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **매력 가격 책정**, 작고 조용한 일을 하고 있다.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: 그것을 $1,200에 책정된 Delta One 대륙 간 좌석과 비교한다 — 깔끔한 정수.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: 누구도 4자리 숫자를 지출하고 누워 있는 좌석에 대해 $1,199를 보고 싶어하지 않는다.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **프리미엄 가격 책정**은 매력 가격 책정이 작동을 멈추는 곳을 차지한다.

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: 같은 항공기.

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: 같은 노선.

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: 같은 날.

segments.src: Four pricing concepts stacked in a single booking screen.
segments.tr: 한 개의 예약 화면에 쌓인 네 가지 가격 책정 개념.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. 가격은 세 가지 방식으로 설정된다 — 비용에서, 경쟁자에서, 또는 고객 가치에서 — 그리고 가치 기반 가격 책정은 보통 가장 수익성이 높다. 스프레드시트가 아니라 구매자로부터 시작하기 때문이다.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. 심리적 가격 책정은 숫자가 어떻게 읽히는지 형성한다: 일상적인 가치를 위한 $9.99, 명품을 위한 깔끔한 $500, 그리고 목표 옵션을 합리적으로 보이게 만드는 미끼나 앵커.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. 가격 차등은 자동 선택(등급, 크기, 선구매) 또는 신원(학생, 노인)을 사용하여 거의 같은 제품에 대해 다른 구매자에게 다른 금액을 부과한다 — 그리고 한 항공기가 동시에 $89 및 $450 승객을 운송하는 방법이다.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A boutique sells a handmade leather bag.
segments.tr: **1.** 한 부티크가 수제 가죽 가방을 판다.

segments.src: The materials and labor cost $80.
segments.tr: 재료와 노동비는 $80이다.

segments.src: The owner researches what customers say the bag is worth to them and prices it at $340.
segments.tr: 소유자는 고객이 가방이 자신들에게 얼마나 가치가 있는지 조사하고 $340에 가격을 책정한다.

segments.src: Which pricing method is this?
segments.tr: 이것은 어떤 가격 책정 방법인가?

segments.src: - A) Cost-based pricing
segments.tr: - A) 원가 기반 가격 책정

segments.src: - B) Competition-based pricing
segments.tr: - B) 경쟁 기반 가격 책정

segments.src: - C) Value-based pricing
segments.tr: - C) 가치 기반 가격 책정

segments.src: - D) Penetration pricing
segments.tr: - D) 침투 가격 책정

segments.src: **2.** A movie theater offers popcorn at Small $4.00, Medium $7.50, and Large $8.00.
segments.tr: **2.** 한 영화관이 팝콘을 소 $4.00, 중 $7.50, 대 $8.00에 제공한다.

segments.src: The medium size sells poorly, but the theater keeps it on the menu anyway.
segments.tr: 중간 크기는 판매가 잘 안 되지만, 극장은 어쨌든 메뉴에 유지한다.

segments.src: What is the medium most likely doing?
segments.tr: 중간은 가장 가능성이 높게 뭘 하고 있는가?

segments.src: - A) Acting as a decoy that makes the Large look like better value
segments.tr: - A) 큰 크기를 더 나은 가치로 보이게 하는 미끼로 작용한다

segments.src: - B) Covering the fixed cost of the popcorn machine
segments.tr: - B) 팝콘 기계의 고정 비용을 충당한다

segments.src: - C) Serving as an example of charm pricing
segments.tr: - C) 매력 가격 책정의 예로서 역할을 한다

segments.src: - D) Preventing price fixing among competing theaters
segments.tr: - D) 경쟁하는 극장들 간의 가격 담합을 방지한다

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Offering a discounted movie ticket to customers over 65 is a form of third-degree price discrimination.
segments.tr: **3.** O/X: 65세 이상의 고객에게 할인된 영화표를 제공하는 것은 3도 가격 차등의 한 형태이다.

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Cost-based pricing** — Setting a price by starting from production cost and adding a markup or target margin.
segments.tr: - **원가 기반 가격 책정** — 생산 비용으로 시작하여 마크업 또는 목표 마진을 추가하여 가격을 설정한다.

segments.src: - **Value-based pricing** — Setting a price from what the product is worth to the customer, independent of what it cost to make.
segments.tr: - **가치 기반 가격 책정** — 제품을 만드는 데 비용이 얼마나 들었는지와 무관하게 고객에게 제품의 가치가 얼마인지에서 가격을 설정한다.

segments.src: - **Charm pricing** — Ending a price just below a round number (e.g., $9.99) so it reads as meaningfully cheaper.

zh.title: [市场营销101 #8] 为什么你的$4.99咖啡其实不只是咖啡

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > 价格是市场营销中唯一能带来收入的部分——其他一切都是支出。本课程涵盖价格如何确定、为什么$9.99看起来比$10便宜，以及同一航班的同一座位如何可能有三种不同的价格。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: 大多数人认为定价是算术问题：加起成本，加上利润，完成。

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: 这是一种真实的方法，但也是最乏味的。

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: 公司确定数字有三种广泛的方式。

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **成本定价。** 从制造成本开始，加上加价。

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: 一家在食材上花费$4且希望有70%食品成本利润率的餐厅价格接近$13。

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: 这很简单安全，但有一个盲点：你的成本与客户无关。

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: 如果没有人想要这道菜的$13价格，数学不会改变。

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **竞争定价。** 看别人怎么收费，相应地定位自己——匹配、略低或故意高于。

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: 加油站几乎实时地这样做。

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: 风险是你把战略外包给对手，如果他们错了，你也就错了。

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **价值定价。** 从另一个角度开始：这对购买者有什么价值？

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: 一副$200的处方眼镜和一副$600的眼镜制造成本可能几乎相同。

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: 差价源于买家对镜架的认知。

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 这是大多数营销人员倾向的方法，因为它从客户开始，而不是从电子表格开始。

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: 然后是第二层：**心理定价** ——数字如何呈现，而不仅仅是它是什么。

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *魅力定价*：$9.99而不是$10。研究普遍显示需求会有小幅但真实的提升，主要是因为我们从左到右阅读，锚定在"9"上。效果很温和，最适用于价值导向的日常购买。

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *威望定价*：整数$500而不是$499。对于奢侈品，整洁的数字传达信心；折扣提示会损害产品。

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *锚定*：在$1,200的笔记本旁展示$799的笔记本使$799看起来合理。你看到的第一个数字设定了心理标准。

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *诱饵效应*：小份爆米花$4，大份$8感觉太贵——直到出现$7.50的中份，大份突然看起来物超所值。中份不是用来卖的；它用来衬托大份。

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: 第三层：**价格歧视** ——对基本相同的商品向不同买家收取不同价格。

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: 听起来有些不当，这个名字也没有帮助，但它通常是合法的，通常能让每个人都受益。

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: 经济学家将其分为三个层级：

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *一级*：每个客户定制价格。在零售业中罕见，在汽车经销店和B2B合同中常见。

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *二级*：价格取决于**你的选择**——尺寸、层级或数量。Costco大包装、Spotify免费版对比高级版、咖啡店的12/16/20盎司杯子。客户自行分类。

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *三级*：价格取决于**你是谁**——学生、老年人或军人折扣；区域定价。

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: 统一的想法：不同的人愿意支付不同的金额，单一价格要么造成收益损失，要么失去客户。

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: 价格歧视让卖家可以捕捉两端的更多价值。

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: 一个值得知道的法律说明：在美国对不同的*消费者*收取不同价格通常是可以的。

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: 《罗宾逊-帕特曼法案》限制了同一商品的*竞争性商业买家*之间的价格歧视，反垄断法禁止*价格固定*——竞争对手就价格达成协议。

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: 这些与老年人折扣是不同的。

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 日常中

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: 预订一班从芝加哥奥黑尔到丹佛的航班，你会在一个屏幕上看到所有三层定价。

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: 航空公司不按成本定价。

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: 一旦飞机飞行，再多载一个乘客的边际成本大约是他们体重的燃油和一罐饮料——大约$30。

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: 然而同一架飞机在同一个星期二的票价范围从$89到$450。

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: 这是**价值定价**与**价格歧视**的结合。

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: 谁在支付$450？

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: 周一早上预订、周四晚上返回、提前八天预订的顾问。

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: 谁在支付$89？

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: 提前七周预订、周二到周六出行、不在意后排中间座位的旅行者。

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: 航空公司从不问"你是商务旅客吗？"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: ——它不需要。

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: 它建立壁垒：提前购买要求、周六晚住宿、改签费用。

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: 商务旅客不会跨越这些壁垒，所以他们自然落入更贵的票价。

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: 这是教科书式的二级价格歧视。

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: 现在看座位地图。

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: 大多数旅客不选经济舱——它不允许手提行李或座位选择。

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: 它主要是为了让$129看起来像是明智的中间选择。

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **诱饵效应**，在现实中。

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
**Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **魅力定价**，默默发挥作用。

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: 对比之下，Delta One跨大陆座位标价$1,200——一个整洁的整数。

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: 没有人在平躺座位上花费四位数价格会想看到$1,199。

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **威望定价**接过魅力定价失效的地方。

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: 同一架飞机。

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: 同一路线。

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: 同一天。

segments.src: Four pricing concepts stacked in a single booking screen.
segments.tr: 四个定价概念叠加在一个预订屏幕上。

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. 价格由三种方式设定——从成本、竞争对手或客户价值——价值定价通常最盈利，因为它从买家开始，而不是电子表格。

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. 心理定价塑造了数字的呈现方式：日常价值用$9.99，奢侈品用整数$500，诱饵或锚定使目标选项看起来合理。

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. 价格歧视对基本相同的产品向不同买家收取不同金额，使用自选（层级、尺寸、提前购买）或身份（学生、老年人）——这就是同一架飞机如何同时载有$89和$450的乘客。

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测问卷

segments.src: **1.** A boutique sells a handmade leather bag.
segments.tr: **1.** 一家精品店出售手工皮包。

segments.src: The materials and labor cost $80.
segments.tr: 材料和劳动力成本$80。

segments.src: The owner researches what customers say the bag is worth to them and prices it at $340.
segments.tr: 店主调查客户认为包值多少钱，并以$340的价格出售。

segments.src: Which pricing method is this?
segments.tr: 这是哪种定价方法？

segments.src: - A) Cost-based pricing
segments.tr: - A) 成本定价

segments.src: - B) Competition-based pricing
segments.tr: - B) 竞争定价

segments.src: - C) Value-based pricing
segments.tr: - C) 价值定价

segments.src: - D) Penetration pricing
segments.tr: - D) 渗透定价

segments.src: **2.** A movie theater offers popcorn at Small $4.00, Medium $7.50, and Large $8.00.
The medium size sells poorly, but the theater keeps it on the menu anyway.
segments.tr: 中份销售不佳，但电影院还是把它放在菜单上。

segments.src: What is the medium most likely doing?
segments.tr: 中份最可能的作用是什么？

segments.src: - A) Acting as a decoy that makes the Large look like better value
segments.tr: - A) 充当诱饵，使大份看起来更划算

segments.src: - B) Covering the fixed cost of the popcorn machine
segments.tr: - B) 覆盖爆米花机器的固定成本

segments.src: - C) Serving as an example of charm pricing
segments.tr: - C) 作为魅力定价的例子

segments.src: - D) Preventing price fixing among competing theaters
segments.tr: - D) 防止竞争电影院之间的价格固定

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Offering a discounted movie ticket to customers over 65 is a form of third-degree price discrimination.
segments.tr: **3.** O/X：向65岁以上的客户提供折扣电影票是三级价格歧视的形式。

segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.tr: यह एक वास्तविक विधि है, लेकिन यह सबसे दिलचस्प नहीं है।

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: कंपनियां किसी संख्या पर पहुंचने के लिए तीन व्यापक तरीके हैं।

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **लागत-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण।** इसे बनाने की लागत से शुरू करें, एक मार्कअप जोड़ें।

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: एक रेस्तरां जो सामग्री पर $4 खर्च करता है और 70% भोजन लागत मार्जिन चाहता है वह $13 के पास उतरता है।

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: यह सरल और सुरक्षित है, और इसका एक अंधा स्थान है: आपकी लागत ग्राहक का कोई व्यवसाय नहीं है।

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: अगर कोई भी $13 पर व्यंजन नहीं चाहता है, तो गणित परवाह नहीं करता है।

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **प्रतिस्पर्धा-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण।** देखें कि बाकी सब कुछ क्या खर्च करता है और अपने आप को उसके विरुद्ध स्थिति दें — मिलान करना, थोड़ा कम, या जानबूझकर ऊपर।

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: गैस स्टेशन लगभग वास्तविक समय में ऐसा करते हैं।

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: जोखिम यह है कि आप अपनी रणनीति को अपने प्रतिद्वंद्वियों को आउटसोर्स करते हैं, और अगर वे गलत हैं, तो आप भी हैं।

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **मूल्य-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण।** दूसरे छोर से शुरू करें: यह खरीदार के लिए क्या मूल्य है?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: एक $200 जोड़ी प्रेस्क्रिप्शन चश्मा और एक $600 जोड़ी का उत्पादन लागत लगभग समान हो सकती है।

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: अंतर यह है कि खरीदार फ्रेम के बारे में क्या मानता है।

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: यह वह विधि है जिसे अधिकांश विपणक धक्का देते हैं, क्योंकि यह स्प्रेडशीट के बजाय ग्राहक के साथ शुरू होता है।

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: फिर दूसरी परत है: **मनोवैज्ञानिक मूल्य निर्धारण** — संख्या कैसे *पढ़ी जाती है*, न कि यह क्या है।

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *आकर्षण मूल्य निर्धारण*: $10 के बजाय $9.99। शोध आम तौर पर मांग में एक छोटी लेकिन वास्तविक वृद्धि दिखाता है, मुख्यतः क्योंकि हम बाएं से दाएं पढ़ते हैं और "9" पर लंगर डालते हैं। प्रभाव मामूली है और मूल्य-संचालित, रोजमर्रा की खरीदारी पर सबसे अच्छी तरह काम करता है।

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *प्रतिष्ठा मूल्य निर्धारण*: $499 के बजाय एक गोल $500। विलासितापूर्ण वस्तुओं के लिए, एक स्वच्छ संख्या आत्मविश्वास का संकेत देती है; छूट संकेत उत्पाद को कम करेगा।

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *लंगर डालना*: एक $1,200 लैपटॉप को $799 के बगल में दिखाना $799 को उचित महसूस कराता है। पहली संख्या जो आप देखते हैं वह मानसिक यार्डस्टिक निर्धारित करती है।

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *डिकॉय प्रभाव*: छोटा पॉपकॉर्न $4, बड़ा $8 एक खिंचाव लगता है — जब तक एक मध्यम $7.50 पर दिखाई न दे और बड़ा अचानक एक सौदा की तरह दिखता है। माध्यम वहां बेचने के लिए नहीं है; यह बड़े को अच्छा दिखाने के लिए है।

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: तीसरी परत: **मूल्य भेदभाव** — विभिन्न खरीदारों को अनिवार्यतः एक ही चीज के लिए अलग-अलग कीमतें वसूल करना।

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: यह संदिग्ध लगता है, और नाम इसमें मदद नहीं करता है, लेकिन यह आमतौर पर कानूनी है और अक्सर सभी को बेहतर बनाता है।

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: अर्थशास्त्री इसे तीन डिग्री में विभाजित करते हैं:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *पहली डिग्री*: प्रति ग्राहक कस्टम मूल्य। खुदरा में दुर्लभ, कार डीलरशिप और B2B अनुबंधों में सामान्य।

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *दूसरी डिग्री*: कीमत इस पर निर्भर करती है कि **आप क्या चुनते हैं** — आकार, स्तर, या मात्रा। कॉस्टको बल्क पैक, स्पॉटिफाई फ्री बनाम प्रीमियम, एक कॉफी दुकान के 12/16/20 औंस कप। ग्राहक खुद को क्रमबद्ध करते हैं।

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *तीसरी डिग्री*: कीमत इस पर निर्भर करती है कि **आप कौन हैं** — छात्र, वरिष्ठ, या सैनिक छूट; क्षेत्रीय मूल्य निर्धारण।

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: एकीकृत विचार: विभिन्न लोग विभिन्न राशि का भुगतान करने के लिए तैयार हैं, और एक एकल मूल्य या तो टेबल पर पैसा छोड़ता है या ग्राहकों को पीछे छोड़ता है।

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: मूल्य भेदभाव एक विक्रेता को दोनों सिरों में अधिक पकड़ने की अनुमति देता है।

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: एक कानूनी नोट जानने योग्य है: विभिन्न *उपभोक्ताओं* को अलग-अलग कीमतें वसूल करना आम तौर पर यूएस में ठीक है।

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: रॉबिंसन-पैटमैन अधिनियम एक ही वस्तु के प्रतिस्पर्धी व्यावसायिक खरीदारों के बीच मूल्य भेदभाव को प्रतिबंधित करता है, और प्रतिविरोधी कानून *मूल्य निर्धारण* को प्रतिबंधित करता है — प्रतिद्वंद्वी कीमतें तय करने पर सहमत हैं।

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: वे वरिष्ठ छूट से अलग चीजें हैं।

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: शिकागो ओ'हारे से डेनवर तक एक उड़ान बुक करें और आप एक स्क्रीन पर तीनों परतें देखेंगे।

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: एयरलाइन लागत के आधार पर मूल्य नहीं देती है।

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: एक बार जब विमान उड़ रहा है, तो एक और यात्री की सीमांत लागत उनके शरीर के वजन के लिए ईंधन और सोडा की एक कैन है — इसे $30 कहते हैं।

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: फिर भी एक ही विमान पर एक ही मंगलवार को $89 से $450 तक किराया।

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: यह **मूल्य-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण** **मूल्य भेदभाव** से मिल रहा है।

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: $450 कौन भुगतान कर रहा है?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: सलाहकार सोमवार सुबह बुकिंग, गुरुवार रात को लौटना, जो आठ दिन पहले बुक करता है।

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: $89 कौन भुगतान कर रहा है?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: यात्री जो सात सप्ताह पहले बुक किया, मंगलवार से शनिवार तक उड़ता है, और मध्य सीट को पीछे की ओर परवाह नहीं करता है।

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: एयरलाइन कभी नहीं पूछती "क्या आप एक व्यावसायिक यात्री हैं?"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — इसकी जरूरत नहीं है।

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: यह बाड़ लगाता है: अग्रिम खरीद आवश्यकताएं, शनिवार-रात की रहें, परिवर्तन शुल्क।

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: व्यावसायिक यात्री उन बाड़ों को कूदेंगे नहीं, इसलिए वे खुद को महंगे किराए में क्रमबद्ध करते हैं।

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: यह पाठ्यपुस्तक दूसरी डिग्री भेदभाव है।

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: अब सीट मानचित्र को देखें।

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: बेसिक इकोनॉमी $89 पर, मुख्य केबिन $129 पर, आरामदायक+ $189 पर।

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: अधिकांश यात्री बेसिक को चुनते नहीं हैं — यह एक कैरी-ऑन या सीट चयन की अनुमति नहीं देता।

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: यह काफी हद तक $129 को समझदारी वाला मध्य बनाने के लिए मौजूद है।

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **डिकॉय प्रभाव**, जंगली में।

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
**Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **आकर्षण मूल्य निर्धारण**, अपने छोटे शांत काम कर रहा है।

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: एक डेल्टा वन महाद्वीपीय सीट की तुलना करें जो $1,200 पर सूचीबद्ध है — एक स्वच्छ गोल संख्या।

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: कोई भी एक झूठ-सपाट सीट पर चार अंक खर्च करना चाहता है $1,199 नहीं देखना।

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **प्रतिष्ठा मूल्य निर्धारण** उस स्थान से ले जाता है जहां आकर्षण मूल्य निर्धारण काम करना बंद कर देता है।

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: एक ही विमान।

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: एक ही मार्ग।

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: एक ही दिन।

segments.src: Four pricing concepts stacked in a single booking screen.
segments.tr: एक एकल बुकिंग स्क्रीन में ढेर लगे चार मूल्य निर्धारण अवधारणाएं।

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3 पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. कीमतें तीन तरीकों से निर्धारित की जाती हैं — लागत से, प्रतिद्वंद्वियों से, या ग्राहक मूल्य से — और मूल्य-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण आमतौर पर सबसे लाभदायक होता है क्योंकि यह स्प्रेडशीट के बजाय खरीदार के साथ शुरू होता है।

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. मनोवैज्ञानिक मूल्य निर्धारण आकार देता है कि एक संख्या कैसे पढ़ी जाती है: रोजमर्रा की मूल्य के लिए $9.99, विलासिता के लिए एक गोल $500, और डिकॉय या लंगर बनाने के लिए लक्ष्य विकल्प उचित दिखता है।

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. मूल्य भेदभाव विभिन्न खरीदारों को लगभग एक ही उत्पाद के लिए अलग-अलग राशि वसूल करता है, आत्म-चयन (स्तर, आकार, अग्रिम खरीद) या पहचान (छात्र, वरिष्ठ) का उपयोग करके — और यह है कि कैसे एक विमान एक बार में $89 और $450 यात्री ले जाता है।

segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व परीक्षा

segments.src: **1.** A boutique sells a handmade leather bag.
segments.tr: **1.** एक बुटीक एक हाथ से बना चमड़े की बैग बेचता है।

segments.src: The materials and labor cost $80.
segments.tr: सामग्री और श्रम की लागत $80 है।

segments.src: The owner researches what customers say the bag is worth to them and prices it at $340.
segments.tr: मालिक अनुसंधान करता है कि ग्राहक बैग को उनके लिए क्या मूल्य कहते हैं और इसे $340 पर कीमत देता है।

segments.tr: यह कौन सी मूल्य निर्धारण विधि है?

segments.src: - A) Cost-based pricing
segments.tr: - A) लागत-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण

segments.src: - B) Competition-based pricing
segments.tr: - B) प्रतिस्पर्धा-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण

segments.src: - C) Value-based pricing
segments.tr: - C) मूल्य-आधारित मूल्य निर्धारण

segments.src: - D) Penetration pricing

es.title: [Marketing 101 #8] Por qué tu café de $4.99 no trata realmente del café

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > El precio es la única parte del marketing que trae dinero — todo lo demás lo gasta. Esta lección cubre cómo se fijan los precios, por qué $9.99 se siente más barato que $10, y cómo el mismo asiento en el mismo vuelo puede costar tres cantidades diferentes.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: La mayoría de las personas piensan que el precio es aritmética: suma tus costos, añade una ganancia, listo.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: Ese es un método real, pero es el menos interesante.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: Hay tres formas generales en que las empresas establecen un número.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **Fijación de precios basada en costos.** Comienza con lo que te cuesta hacer la cosa, añade un margen.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: Un restaurante que gasta $4 en ingredientes y quiere un margen de costo de alimentos del 70% llega cerca de $13.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: Es simple y seguro, y tiene un punto ciego: tus costos no son asunto del cliente.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: Si nadie quiere el plato a $13, las matemáticas no se preocupan.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **Fijación de precios basada en competencia.** Mira lo que cobran los demás y posiciónate contra ello — igualar, un poco menos, o deliberadamente más.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: Las gasolineras hacen esto casi en tiempo real.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: El riesgo es que externalices tu estrategia a tus rivales, y si están equivocados, tú también.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **Fijación de precios basada en valor.** Comienza en el otro extremo: ¿cuánto vale esto para el comprador?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: Un par de anteojos de prescripción de $200 y un par de $600 pueden costar casi lo mismo de producir.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: La brecha es lo que el comprador cree sobre la montura.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Este es el método hacia el que la mayoría de los especialistas en marketing empujan, porque comienza con el cliente en lugar de la hoja de cálculo.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: Luego está la segunda capa: **fijación de precios psicológica** — cómo se *lee* el número, no solo qué es.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *Fijación de precios de encanto*: $9.99 en lugar de $10. La investigación generalmente muestra un pequeño pero real aumento en la demanda, principalmente porque leemos de izquierda a derecha y nos anclamos en el "9". El efecto es modesto y funciona mejor en compras cotidianas orientadas al valor.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *Fijación de precios de prestigio*: un redondo $500 en lugar de $499. Para bienes de lujo, un número limpio señala confianza; la pista de descuento socavaría el producto.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *Anclaje*: mostrar una computadora portátil de $1,200 junto a una de $799 hace que $799 se sienta razonable. El primer número que ves establece la vara mental.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *Efecto señuelo*: palomitas pequeñas $4, grandes $8 se siente como un estiramiento — hasta que aparece un medio a $7.50 y lo grande de repente se ve como una ganga. El medio no está allí para vender; está allí para que lo grande se vea bien.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: La tercera capa: **discriminación de precios** — cobrar a diferentes compradores precios diferentes por esencialmente lo mismo.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Suena turbio, y el nombre no ayuda, pero generalmente es legal y a menudo hace que todos estén mejor.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Los economistas lo clasifican en tres grados:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *Primer grado*: un precio personalizado por cliente. Raro en retail, común en concesionarios de automóviles y contratos B2B.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *Segundo grado*: el precio depende de **lo que elijas** — tamaño, nivel o cantidad. Paquetes a granel de Costco, Spotify Free vs. Premium, tazas de 12/16/20 oz de una cafetería. Los clientes se clasifican a sí mismos.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *Tercer grado*: el precio depende de **quién eres** — descuentos para estudiantes, personas mayores o militares; fijación de precios regional.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: La idea unificadora: diferentes personas están dispuestas a pagar diferentes cantidades, y un único precio deja dinero sobre la mesa o deja clientes atrás.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: La discriminación de precios permite a un vendedor capturar más de ambos extremos.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Una nota legal que vale la pena conocer: cobrar precios diferentes a diferentes *consumidores* generalmente está bien en los EE.UU.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: La Ley Robinson-Patman restringe la discriminación de precios entre *compradores comerciales competidores* de la misma mercancía, y la ley antimonopolio prohíbe *fijación de precios* — competidores que acuerdan sobre precios.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: Esas son cosas diferentes de un descuento para personas mayores.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: Reserva un vuelo de Chicago O'Hare a Denver y verás las tres capas en una pantalla.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: La aerolínea no fija precios por costo.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: Una vez que el avión está volando, el costo marginal de un pasajero más es aproximadamente el combustible para su peso corporal y una lata de refresco — digamos $30.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, las tarifas oscilan entre $89 y $450 en la misma aeronave el mismo martes.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: Eso es **fijación de precios basada en valor** encontrándose con **discriminación de precios**.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: ¿Quién está pagando $450?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: El consultor que reserva lunes por la mañana, regresando jueves por la noche, quien reservó con ocho días de anticipación.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: ¿Quién está pagando $89?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: El viajero que reservó siete semanas de anticipación, vuela de martes a sábado, y no le importa un asiento del medio en la parte trasera.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: La aerolínea nunca pregunta "¿eres un viajero de negocios?"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — no tiene que hacerlo.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: Construye cercas: requisitos de compra anticipada, estadías de sábado por la noche, cargos por cambios.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: Los viajeros de negocios no saltarán esas cercas, por lo que se clasifican a sí mismos en la tarifa cara.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: Esa es discriminación de segundo grado de manual.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: Ahora mira el mapa de asientos.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: Economía Básica a $89, Cabina Principal a $129, Comfort+ a $189.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: La mayoría de los viajeros no eligen Básica — no permite equipaje de mano o selección de asiento.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: Existe en gran medida para que $129 se sienta como el medio sensato.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **Efecto señuelo**, en la naturaleza.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: Y la tarifa se lee como $129, no $130.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **Fijación de precios de encanto**, haciendo su pequeño trabajo silencioso.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: Compara eso con un asiento transcontinental Delta One cotizado a $1,200 — un número redondo limpio.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: Nadie que gaste cuatro cifras en un asiento acostado quiere ver $1,199.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **Fijación de precios de prestigio** toma el relevo donde la fijación de precios de encanto deja de funcionar.

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: Mismo avión.

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: Misma ruta.

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: Mismo día.

segments.src: Four pricing concepts stacked in a single booking screen.
segments.tr: Cuatro conceptos de precios apilados en una pantalla de reserva única.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. Los precios se fijan de tres formas — a partir de costos, de competidores o del valor del cliente — y la fijación de precios basada en valor generalmente es la más rentable porque comienza con el comprador, no con la hoja de cálculo.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. La fijación de precios psicológica da forma a cómo se lee un número: $9.99 para valor cotidiano, un redondo $500 para lujo, y señuelos o anclas para que la opción objetivo se vea razonable.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. La discriminación de precios cobra a diferentes compradores diferentes cantidades por casi el mismo producto, utilizando auto-selección (niveles, tamaños, compra anticipada) o identidad (estudiante, mayor) — y es cómo un avión lleva pasajeros de $89 y $450 a la vez.

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **Cost-based pricing** — Setting a price by starting from production cost and adding a markup or target margin.
segments.tr: - **Fijación de precios basada en costos** — Establecer un precio comenzando desde el costo de producción y añadiendo un margen o margen objetivo.

segments.src: - **Value-based pricing** — Setting a price from what the product is worth to the customer, independent of what it cost to make.
segments.tr: - **Fijación de precios basada en valor** — Establecer un precio a partir de lo que el producto vale para el cliente, independientemente de lo que costó hacer.

segments.src: - **Charm pricing** — Ending a price just below a round number (e.g., $9.99) so it reads as meaningfully cheaper.
segments.tr: - **Fijación de precios de encanto** — Terminar un precio justo por debajo de un número redondo (p. ej., $9.99) para que se lea como significativamente más barato.

segments.src: - **Anchoring** — The tendency to judge a price against the first number encountered, which becomes a mental reference point.

ar.title: [Marketing 101 #8] لماذا لا يتعلق قهوتك بـ $4.99 بالقهوة حقاً

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > السعر هو الجزء الوحيد من التسويق الذي يجلب المال — كل شيء آخر ينفقه. يغطي هذا الدرس كيفية تحديد الأسعار، ولماذا يبدو $9.99 أرخص من $10، وكيف يمكن لنفس المقعد على نفس الرحلة أن يكلف ثلاث مبالغ مختلفة.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## المفاهيم اليوم

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: يعتقد معظم الناس أن التسعير هو حسابات: اجمع تكاليفك، أضف ربحاً، وانتهي.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: هذه طريقة واحدة حقيقية، لكنها الأقل إثارة للاهتمام.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: هناك ثلاث طرق عريضة يستقر عليها الشركات على رقم.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **التسعير على أساس التكلفة.** ابدأ بما يكلفك لصنع الشيء، أضف هامشاً.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: مطعم ينفق $4 على المكونات ويريد هامش تكلفة غذائية بنسبة 70% يصل إلى حوالي $13.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: إنها بسيطة وآمنة، وفيها عمى: تكاليفك لا تهم العميل.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: إذا لم يرغب أحد في الطبق بـ $13، فإن الحسابات لا تهتم.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **التسعير على أساس المنافسة.** انظر إلى ما يفرضه الآخرون وضع نفسك في مقابله — المطابقة، أقل قليلاً، أو متعمداً أعلى.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: محطات الغاز تفعل هذا في الوقت الفعلي تقريباً.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: الخطر هو أنك تفوض استراتيجيتك لمنافسيك، وإذا أخطأوا، فأنت أيضاً.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **التسعير على أساس القيمة.** ابدأ من الطرف الآخر: كم تساوي هذه للمشتري؟

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: قد تكلف نظارة طبية بقيمة $200 ونظارة بقيمة $600 تقريباً نفس التكلفة للإنتاج.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: الفجوة هي ما يعتقده المشتري عن الإطار.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: هذه هي الطريقة التي يدفع نحوها معظم المسوقين، لأنها تبدأ بالعميل بدلاً من جدول البيانات.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: ثم هناك الطبقة الثانية: **التسعير النفسي** — كيف يبدو الرقم، وليس ما هو فقط.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *التسعير الساحر*: $9.99 بدلاً من $10. يظهر البحث عموماً ارتفاعاً صغيراً لكن حقيقياً في الطلب، في الغالب لأننا نقرأ من اليسار إلى اليمين ونرسي على "9." التأثير متواضع ويعمل بشكل أفضل على المشتريات اليومية المدفوعة بالقيمة.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *التسعير المرموق*: $500 مستديرة بدلاً من $499. بالنسبة للسلع الفاخرة، يشير الرقم النظيف إلى الثقة؛ إشارة الخصم ستضعف المنتج.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *الإرساء*: إظهار كمبيوتر محمول بقيمة $1,200 بجانب واحد بقيمة $799 يجعل الـ $799 يبدو معقولاً. الرقم الأول الذي تراه يحدد المقياس الذهني.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *تأثير الطعم*: فشار صغير $4، كبير $8 يبدو امتداداً — حتى يظهر وسط بـ $7.50 والكبير فجأة يبدو كصفقة جيدة. الوسط ليس هناك للبيع؛ إنه هناك لجعل الكبير يبدو جيداً.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: الطبقة الثالثة: **التمييز السعري** — فرض أسعار مختلفة على مشترين مختلفين لنفس الشيء بشكل أساسي.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: يبدو الأمر مريباً، والاسم لا يساعد، لكنه عادة ما يكون قانونياً وغالباً ما يجعل الجميع أفضل حالاً.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: يصنفها الاقتصاديون إلى ثلاث درجات:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *الدرجة الأولى*: سعر مخصص لكل عميل. نادر في البيع بالتجزئة، شائع في وكالات السيارات وعقود B2B.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *الدرجة الثانية*: السعر يعتمد على **ما تختاره** — الحجم، المستوى، أو الكمية. حزم كوستكو السائبة، Spotify المجاني مقابل Premium، أكواب المقهى 12/16/20 أونصة. يصنف العملاء أنفسهم.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *الدرجة الثالثة*: السعر يعتمد على **من أنت** — طالب، كبير السن، أو خصومات عسكرية؛ الأسعار الإقليمية.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: الفكرة الموحدة: الناس المختلفون على استعداد لدفع مبالغ مختلفة، وسعر واحد إما يترك المال على الطاولة أو يترك العملاء وراءه.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: التمييز السعري يسمح للبائع بالاستيلاء على المزيد من كلا الطرفين.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: ملاحظة قانونية تستحق المعرفة: فرض أسعار مختلفة على المستهلكين المختلفين عموماً بخير في الولايات المتحدة.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: يقيد قانون Robinson-Patman التمييز السعري بين المشترين الذين يتنافسون على نفس السلعة، ويحظر قانون مكافحة الاحتكار *تحديد الأسعار* — متنافسون يتفقون على الأسعار.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: هذه أشياء مختلفة عن خصم كبار السن.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: احجز رحلة من O'Hare بشيكاغو إلى دنفر وستشهد الطبقات الثلاث على شاشة واحدة.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: لا تسعر الخطوط الجوية بالتكلفة.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: بمجرد أن تحلق الطائرة، التكلفة الهامشية لراكب واحد إضافي تقريباً هي الوقود لوزن جسمهم وعلبة صودا — اجعلها $30.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: لكن الأسعار تتراوح من $89 إلى $450 على نفس الطائرة في نفس يوم الثلاثاء.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: هذا هو **التسعير على أساس القيمة** يلتقي **التمييز السعري**.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: من يدفع $450؟

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: المستشار الذي يحجز صباح يوم الاثنين، يعود مساء يوم الخميس، الذي حجز قبل ثمانية أيام.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: من يدفع $89؟

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: المسافر الذي حجز قبل سبعة أسابيع، يطير من الثلاثاء إلى السبت، ولا يمانع المقعد الأوسط في الخلف.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: الخطوط الجوية لا تسأل "هل أنت مسافر أعمال؟"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — لا تحتاج.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: تبني أسواراً: متطلبات الشراء المسبق، إقامات يوم السبت، رسوم التغيير.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: لن يقفز مسافرو الأعمال فوق تلك الأسوار، لذلك يصنفون أنفسهم في الأسعار الباهظة.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: هذا تمييز من الدرجة الثانية من كتاب اللعبة.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: الآن انظر إلى خريطة المقاعد.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: Basic Economy بـ $89، Main Cabin بـ $129، Comfort+ بـ $189.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: معظم المسافرين لا يختارون Basic — لا تسمح بحقيبة يد أو اختيار المقعد.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: إنها موجودة بشكل أساسي لجعل $129 تبدو وسطاً معقولاً.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **تأثير الطعم**، في البرية.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: والسعر يقرأ $129، وليس $130.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **التسعير الساحر**، يقوم بعمله الهادئ الصغير.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: قارن ذلك بمقعد Delta One عابر القارات المدرج بـ $1,200 — رقم مستدير نظيف.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: لا أحد ينفق أربعة أرقام على مقعد مسطح يريد أن يرى $1,199.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **التسعير المرموق** يستولي حيث يتوقف التسعير الساحر عن العمل.

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: نفس الطائرة.

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: نفس الطريق.

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: نفس اليوم.

segments.src: Four pricing concepts stacked in a single booking screen.
segments.tr: أربعة مفاهيم تسعير مكدسة على شاشة حجز واحدة.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## ملخص 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. تُحدد الأسعار بثلاث طرق — من التكاليف أو المنافسين أو قيمة العميل — والتسعير على أساس القيمة عادة ما يكون الأكثر ربحية لأنه يبدأ بالمشتري وليس بجدول البيانات.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. التسعير النفسي يشكل كيفية قراءة الرقم: $9.99 للقيمة اليومية، $500 مستديرة للسلع الفاخرة، والطعوم أو الإرساء لجعل الخيار المستهدف يبدو معقولاً.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. التمييز السعري يفرض مبالغ مختلفة على مشترين مختلفين لمنتج متشابه تقريباً، باستخدام الاختيار الذاتي (مستويات وأحجام والشراء المسبق) أو الهوية (طالب وكبير سن) — وهذا هو كيف تحمل طائرة واحدة ركاباً بـ $89 و$450 في نفس الوقت.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: **1.** تبيع بوتيك حقيبة جلدية مصنوعة يدوياً.

segments.src: The materials and labor cost $80.
segments.tr: تكلف المواد والعمل $80.

segments.src: The owner researches what customers say the bag is worth to them and prices it at $340.
segments.tr: يبحث المالك عما يقوله العملاء الحقيبة تستحق وسعرها $340.

segments.src: Which pricing method is this?
segments.tr: أي طريقة تسعير هذه؟

segments.src: - A) Cost-based pricing
segments.tr: - أ) التسعير على أساس التكلفة

segments.src: - B) Competition-based pricing

segments.src: - C) Value-based pricing
segments.tr: - ج) التسعير على أساس القيمة

segments.src: - D) Penetration pricing
segments.tr: - د) التسعير الاختراقي

segments.src: **2.** A movie theater offers popcorn at Small $4.00, Medium $7.50, and Large $8.00.
segments.tr: **2.** يقدم سينما الفشار بـ Small $4.00، Medium $7.50، و Large $8.00.

segments.src: The medium size sells poorly, but the theater keeps it on the menu anyway.
segments.tr: لا يبيع الحجم الوسط بشكل جيد، لكن السينما تحتفظ به في القائمة على أي حال.

segments.src: What is the medium most likely doing?
segments.tr: ماذا يفعل الحجم الوسط في الغالب؟

segments.src: - A) Acting as a decoy that makes the Large look like better value
segments.tr: - أ) بمثابة طعم يجعل Large يبدو قيمة أفضل

segments.src: - B) Covering the fixed cost of the popcorn machine
segments.tr: - ب) تغطية التكلفة الثابتة لآلة الفشار

segments.src: - C) Serving as an example of charm pricing
segments.tr: - ج) بمثابة مثال على التسعير الساحر

segments.src: - D) Preventing price fixing among competing theaters
segments.tr: - د) منع تحديد الأسعار بين السينما المتنافسة

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Offering a discounted movie ticket to customers over 65 is a form of third-degree price discrimination.
segments.tr: **3.** صح أم خطأ: تقديم تذكرة سينما مخفضة للعملاء فوق 65 هو شكل من أشكال التمييز السعري من الدرجة الثالثة.
