fr.title: [Marketing 101 #8] Pourquoi Votre Café à 4,99 $ N'Est Vraiment Pas une Question de Café

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > Le prix est la seule partie du marketing qui rapporte de l'argent — tout le reste la dépense. Cette leçon explique comment les prix sont fixés, pourquoi 9,99 $ semble moins cher que 10 $, et comment le même siège sur le même vol peut coûter trois montants différents.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: La plupart des gens pensent que la tarification est une simple arithmétique : additionnez vos coûts, ajoutez un profit, c'est fait.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: C'est une véritable méthode, mais c'est la moins intéressante.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: Il existe trois grandes façons dont les entreprises arrivent à un chiffre.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **Tarification basée sur les coûts.** Commencez par ce qu'il vous coûte de fabriquer le produit, puis ajoutez une marge bénéficiaire.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: Un restaurant qui dépense 4 $ en ingrédients et veut une marge de coût alimentaire de 70 % arrive à environ 13 $.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: C'est simple et sûr, et cela a un point aveugle : vos coûts ne regardent pas le client.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: Si personne ne veut le plat à 13 $, les mathématiques s'en fichent.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **Tarification basée sur la concurrence.** Regardez ce que tous les autres facturent et positionnez-vous par rapport à cela — en correspondant, légèrement en dessous, ou délibérément au-dessus.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: Les stations-service le font en quasi-temps réel.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: Le risque est que vous sous-traitiez votre stratégie à vos rivaux, et s'ils se trompent, vous aussi.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **Tarification basée sur la valeur.** Commencez par l'autre bout : que vaut cela pour l'acheteur ?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: Une paire de lunettes de prescription à 200 $ et une paire à 600 $ peuvent coûter à peu près la même chose à produire.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: L'écart est ce que l'acheteur croit à propos de la monture.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: C'est la méthode vers laquelle la plupart des spécialistes du marketing poussent, car elle commence par le client au lieu du tableur.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: Puis vient la deuxième couche : **la tarification psychologique** — comment le nombre *se lit*, pas seulement ce qu'il est.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *Tarification séduisante* : 9,99 $ au lieu de 10 $. La recherche montre généralement une légère mais réelle augmentation de la demande, surtout parce que nous lisons de gauche à droite et nous ancrons sur le « 9 ». L'effet est modeste et fonctionne mieux sur les achats quotidiens axés sur la valeur.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *Tarification de prestige* : un beau 500 $ plutôt que 499 $. Pour les biens de luxe, un nombre rond signale la confiance ; le signal de réduction nuirait au produit.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *Ancrage* : montrer un ordinateur portable à 1 200 $ à côté d'un à 799 $ rend le 799 $ raisonnable. Le premier nombre que vous voyez fixe votre étalon mental.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *Effet de leurre* : un petit pop-corn à 4 $, un grand à 8 $ semble excessif — jusqu'à ce qu'un moyen apparaisse à 7,50 $ et que le grand semble soudain être une bonne affaire. Le moyen n'existe pas pour se vendre ; il existe pour faire ressembler le grand à une bonne affaire.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: La troisième couche : **la discrimination des prix** — facturer à différents acheteurs des prix différents pour essentiellement la même chose.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Cela semble louche, et le nom n'aide pas, mais c'est généralement légal et rend souvent tout le monde mieux loti.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Les économistes la classent en trois degrés :

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *Premier degré* : un prix personnalisé par client. Rare dans le détail, courant dans les concessionnaires automobiles et les contrats B2B.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *Deuxième degré* : le prix dépend de **ce que vous choisissez** — taille, niveau ou quantité. Les packs en vrac de Costco, Spotify Gratuit vs. Premium, les tasses 12/16/20 oz d'un café. Les clients se trient eux-mêmes.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *Troisième degré* : le prix dépend de **qui vous êtes** — réductions pour étudiants, seniors ou militaires ; tarification régionale.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: L'idée unificatrice : les gens différents sont prêts à payer des montants différents, et un prix unique laisse soit de l'argent sur la table, soit laisse des clients de côté.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: La discrimination des prix permet à un vendeur de capturer plus des deux extrémités.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Une note juridique à connaître : facturer des prix différents à différents *consommateurs* est généralement acceptable aux États-Unis.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: La Loi Robinson-Patman restreint la discrimination des prix entre les *acheteurs professionnels concurrents* de la même marchandise, et la loi antitrust interdit la *fixation des prix* — les concurrents s'accordant sur les prix.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: Ce sont des choses différentes d'une réduction pour les aînés.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: Réservez un vol de Chicago O'Hare à Denver et vous verrez les trois couches en un seul écran.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: La compagnie aérienne ne fixe pas les prix en fonction des coûts.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: Une fois l'avion en vol, le coût marginal d'un passager supplémentaire est à peu près le carburant pour son poids corporel et une canette de soda — disons 30 $.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: Pourtant, les tarifs vont de 89 $ à 450 $ sur le même aéronef le même mardi.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: C'est la **tarification basée sur la valeur** rencontrant la **discrimination des prix**.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: Qui paie 450 $ ?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: Le consultant réservant lundi matin, retournant jeudi soir, qui a réservé huit jours à l'avance.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: Qui paie 89 $ ?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: Le voyageur qui a réservé sept semaines à l'avance, vole mardi à samedi, et ne se dérange pas d'un siège du milieu à l'arrière.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: La compagnie aérienne ne demande jamais « êtes-vous un voyageur d'affaires ? »

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — elle n'a pas besoin de le faire.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: Elle construit des barrières : exigences d'achat à l'avance, séjours le samedi soir, frais de modification.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: Les voyageurs d'affaires ne franchiront pas ces barrières, donc ils se classent eux-mêmes dans le tarif cher.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: C'est un exemple classique de discrimination du deuxième degré.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: Maintenant, regardez la carte des sièges.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: Économie de base à 89 $, Cabine principale à 129 $, Confort+ à 189 $.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: La plupart des voyageurs ne choisissent pas Économie de base — elle ne permet pas de bagage à main ou de sélection de siège.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: Elle existe surtout pour faire de 129 $ l'option sensée du milieu.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **Effet de leurre**, dans la nature sauvage.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: Et le tarif se lit 129 $, pas 130 $.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **Tarification séduisante**, faisant son petit travail tranquille.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: Comparez cela à un siège Delta One transcontinental affiché à 1 200 $ — un nombre rond et propre.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: Personne dépensant quatre chiffres sur un siège semi-couché ne veut voir 1 199 $.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **La tarification de prestige** prend le relais là où la tarification séduisante cesse de fonctionner.

segments.src: Same plane.
segments.tr: Même avion.

segments.src: Same route.
segments.tr: Même route.

segments.src: Same day.
segments.tr: Même jour.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. Les prix sont fixés de trois façons — à partir des coûts, des concurrents ou de la valeur client — et la tarification basée sur la valeur est généralement la plus rentable car elle commence par l'acheteur, pas par le tableur.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. La tarification psychologique façonne la façon dont un nombre est lu : 9,99 $ pour la valeur quotidienne, un beau 500 $ pour le luxe, et des leurres ou des ancrages pour faire ressembler l'option cible à quelque chose de raisonnable.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. La discrimination des prix facture à différents acheteurs des montants différents pour un produit presque identique, en utilisant l'auto-sélection (niveaux, tailles, achat à l'avance) ou l'identité (étudiant, senior) — et c'est ainsi qu'un avion porte des passagers à 89 $ et 450 $ à la fois.

segments.tr: - *Efeito isco*: pipoca pequena $4, grande $8 parece um exagero — até que um médio aparece por $7,50 e o grande de repente parece uma pechincha. O médio não está lá para vender; está lá para fazer o grande parecer bom.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: A terceira camada: **discriminação de preço** — cobrar de diferentes compradores preços diferentes pela essencialmente mesma coisa.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Soa obscuro, e o nome não ajuda, mas é geralmente legal e frequentemente deixa todos em melhor situação.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Economistas a classificam em três graus:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *Primeiro grau*: um preço personalizado por cliente. Raro no varejo, comum em concessionárias de carros e contratos B2B.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *Segundo grau*: o preço depende do **que você escolhe** — tamanho, nível ou quantidade. Pacotes a granel da Costco, Spotify Grátis vs. Premium, copos de 12/16/20 oz de uma cafeteria. Os clientes se separam sozinhos.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *Terceiro grau*: o preço depende de **quem você é** — descontos para estudante, idoso ou militar; preços regionais.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: A ideia unificadora: diferentes pessoas estão dispostas a pagar quantidades diferentes, e um preço único deixa dinheiro na mesa ou deixa clientes para trás.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: A discriminação de preço permite que um vendedor capture mais das duas extremidades.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Uma nota legal que vale a pena conhecer: cobrar preços diferentes de diferentes *consumidores* é geralmente aceitável nos EUA.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: A Lei Robinson-Patman restringe a discriminação de preço entre *compradores empresariais concorrentes* da mesma mercadoria, e a lei antitruste proíbe *fixação de preço* — concorrentes concordando sobre preços.

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.

segments.tr: - **Precificação baseada em custos** — Definir um preço começando a partir do custo de produção e adicionando uma margem ou margem de alvo.

segments.src: - **Value-based pricing** — Setting a price from what the product is worth to the customer, independent of what it cost to make.
segments.tr: - **Precificação baseada em valor** — Definir um preço a partir do que o produto vale para o cliente, independentemente do que custou fazer.

segments.src: - **Charm pricing** — Ending a price just below a round number (e.g., $9.99) so it reads as meaningfully cheaper.

segments.src: - **Anchoring** — The tendency to judge a price against the first number encountered, which becomes a mental reference point.
segments.tr: - **Ancoragem** — A tendência de julgar um preço contra o primeiro número encontrado, que se torna um ponto de referência mental.

segments.src: - **Price discrimination** — Charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same product, based on what they choose (second degree) or who they are (third degree).

in.title: [Marketing 101 #8] Mengapa Kopi Anda Seharga $4.99 Sebenarnya Bukan Tentang Kopi

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > Harga adalah satu-satunya bagian dari pemasaran yang menghasilkan uang — semuanya yang lain menghabiskan uang. Pelajaran ini mencakup cara harga ditetapkan, mengapa $9.99 terasa lebih murah dari $10, dan bagaimana kursi yang sama di penerbangan yang sama dapat memiliki tiga harga berbeda.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar orang berpikir penetapan harga adalah aritmatika: jumlahkan biaya Anda, tambahkan keuntungan, selesai.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: Itu adalah satu metode nyata, tetapi itu adalah yang paling tidak menarik.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: Ada tiga cara luas perusahaan menetapkan angka.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **Penetapan harga berbasis biaya.** Mulai dengan berapa biaya Anda untuk membuat barang tersebut, tambahkan markup.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: Restoran yang mengeluarkan $4 untuk bahan dan menginginkan margin biaya makanan 70% mendapat harga sekitar $13.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: Ini sederhana dan aman, dan memiliki titik buta: biaya Anda bukan urusan pelanggan.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: Jika tidak ada yang menginginkan hidangan seharga $13, matematika tidak peduli.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **Penetapan harga berbasis kompetisi.** Lihat apa yang dikenakan orang lain dan posisikan diri Anda melawannya — menyamakan, sedikit di bawah, atau sengaja di atas.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: Stasiun gas melakukan ini secara hampir real-time.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: Risikonya adalah Anda mengalihkan strategi Anda kepada pesaing, dan jika mereka salah, Anda juga.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **Penetapan harga berbasis nilai.** Mulai dari ujung lain: berapa nilai ini bagi pembeli?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: Sepasang kacamata resep $200 dan sepasang $600 mungkin memiliki biaya produksi yang hampir sama.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: Perbedaannya adalah apa yang pembeli percayai tentang bingkainya.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Ini adalah metode yang didorong oleh sebagian besar pemasar, karena dimulai dengan pelanggan bukan spreadsheet.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: Kemudian ada lapisan kedua: **penetapan harga psikologis** — bagaimana angka itu *dibaca*, bukan hanya apa adanya.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 daripada $10. Penelitian secara umum menunjukkan peningkatan kecil tetapi nyata dalam permintaan, sebagian besar karena kita membaca dari kiri ke kanan dan mengankar pada "9." Efeknya sederhana dan paling baik untuk pembelian yang didorong nilai, sehari-hari.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *Prestige pricing*: angka bulat $500 daripada $499. Untuk barang mewah, angka yang bersih menunjukkan kepercayaan; isyarat diskon akan merusak produk.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *Anchoring*: menampilkan laptop $1,200 di sebelah yang $799 membuat yang $799 terasa wajar. Angka pertama yang Anda lihat menetapkan standar mental.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *Efek umpan*: popcorn kecil $4, besar $8 terasa berlebihan — sampai sedang muncul di $7.50 dan yang besar tiba-tiba terlihat seperti penawaran. Sedang tidak ada untuk dijual; itu ada untuk membuat yang besar terlihat bagus.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: Lapisan ketiga: **diskriminasi harga** — mengenakan harga berbeda kepada pembeli berbeda untuk hal yang pada dasarnya sama.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Ini terdengar mencurigakan, dan namanya tidak membantu, tetapi biasanya legal dan sering membuat semua orang lebih baik.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Ekonom mengurutkannya menjadi tiga derajat:

segments.tr: - *Derajat pertama*: harga khusus per pelanggan. Jarang di ritel, umum di dealer mobil dan kontrak B2B.

segments.tr: - *Derajat ketiga*: harga tergantung pada **siapa Anda** — mahasiswa, senior, atau diskon militer; penetapan harga regional.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Satu catatan hukum yang perlu diketahui: mengenakan harga berbeda kepada *konsumen* berbeda secara umum baik di A.S.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. Penetapan harga psikologis membentuk bagaimana angka dibaca: $9.99 untuk nilai sehari-hari, $500 bulat untuk kemewahan, dan umpan atau jangkar untuk membuat opsi target terlihat wajar.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.

ja.title: [マーケティング 101 #8] あなたの$4.99のコーヒーが本当はコーヒーについてではない理由

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > マーケティングでお金を生み出す唯一の要素は価格です。他はすべてお金を消費します。このレッスンでは、価格がどのように設定されるのか、なぜ$9.99が$10より安く見えるのか、そして同じフライトの同じ座席がいかに3つの異なる価格になるのかについてカバーしています。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: ほとんどの人は価格設定が算術だと考えています。コストを合算して、利益を上乗せして、完了です。

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: それは1つの本当の方法ですが、最も興味深くない方法です。

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: 企業が数字に到達する3つの大きな方法があります。

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **コスト基準価格設定。** その物を作るのにかかるコストから始めて、マークアップを加えます。

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: 材料に$4を費やし、70%の食品原価率を目指すレストランは、$13付近の価格になります。

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: シンプルで安全ですが、盲点があります。あなたのコストは顧客には関係ありません。

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: $13でその料理を誰も欲しくなければ、数学は気にしません。

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **競争基準価格設定。** 他者がどの程度の価格を設定しているかを見て、それに対して自分の立場を決めます。一致させるか、わずかに低くするか、意図的に高くするか。

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: ガソリンスタンドはほぼリアルタイムでこれを行います。

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: リスクは、あなたの戦略をライバルに丸投げしてしまい、彼らが間違っていたら、あなたも間違っているということです。

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **価値基準価格設定。** 反対側から始めます。これは購入者にとってどのくらいの価値がありますか？

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: $200の処方眼鏡と$600の眼鏡は、ほぼ同じコストで製造されるかもしれません。

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: その差は、購入者がフレームについて何を信じているかです。

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: これはほとんどのマーケターが推し進める方法です。スプレッドシートではなく、顧客から始まるからです。

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: 次が2番目のレイヤーです。**心理的価格設定** —数字がどのように*読まれるか*、それが何であるかだけではなく。

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *チャーム価格設定*: $10の代わりに$9.99。研究は一般的に需要が小さいが実際に上昇することを示しています。主に左から右に読み、「9」にアンカーするからです。効果は控えめで、価値重視の日常購入に最適に機能します。

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *プレステージ価格設定*: $499ではなくキレイな$500。高級品の場合、きれいな数字は自信を信号します。割引的な表現は製品を損なわせるでしょう。

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *アンカリング*: $1,200のラップトップの隣に$799のラップトップを置くと、$799が合理的に感じます。最初に見える数字が、心理的な基準点になります。

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *デコイ効果*: 小$4、大$8は無理な価格に見えます。中サイズが$7.50で出現するまでは。すると大が急に割安に見えます。中は売れることが目的ではなく、大を割安に見せるために存在しています。

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: 3番目のレイヤー: **価格差別** —本質的に同じものについて異なる購入者に異なる価格を請求すること。

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: 怪しく聞こえ、その名前も印象的ではありませんが、通常は合法であり、多くの場合、すべての人にとってより良い結果になります。

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: 経済学者はこれを3つの段階に分類します:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *第一段階*: 顧客ごとのカスタム価格。小売では稀ですが、自動車販売店やB2B契約では一般的です。

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *第二段階*: 価格は**あなたが選ぶもの**に左右されます。サイズ、階層、数量です。Costcoの大箱商品、Spotify Free対Premium、コーヒーショップの12/16/20オンスのカップ。顧客が自分たちを振り分けます。

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *第三段階*: 価格は**あなたが誰であるか**に左右されます。学生、シニア、軍人割引。地域別価格。

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: 統一のコンセプト: 異なる人々は異なる金額を支払う意思があり、単一の価格ではテーブルにお金を残すか、顧客を失うかのどちらかになります。

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: 価格差別により、売り手は両端からより多くを獲得できます。

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: 知る価値のある法的注記: 異なる*消費者*に異なる価格を請求することは、通常、米国では問題ありません。

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: Robinson-Patman法は、同じ商品の*競争する企業買い手*間の価格差別を制限し、独占禁止法は*価格カルテル*を禁止しています。競合他社が価格に合意するということです。

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: これらはシニア割引とは別の話です。

segments.tr: ## 日常の中で

de.title: [Marketing 101 #8] Warum dein $4.99-Kaffee eigentlich nichts mit Kaffee zu tun hat

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > Der Preis ist der einzige Teil des Marketings, der Geld hereinbringt — alles andere kostet es. Diese Lektion behandelt, wie Preise festgelegt werden, warum $9.99 günstiger wirkt als $10, und wie der gleiche Sitz auf demselben Flug drei verschiedene Preise kosten kann.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Das Konzept von heute

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: Die meisten Menschen denken, dass Preisgestaltung Arithmetik ist: addiere deine Kosten, schlage einen Gewinn drauf, fertig.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: Das ist eine echte Methode, aber die am wenigsten interessante.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: Es gibt drei breite Wege, wie Unternehmen sich auf eine Zahl einigen.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **Kostenbasierte Preisgestaltung.** Beginne mit dem, was es dich kostet, die Sache herzustellen, und schlage einen Aufschlag auf.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: Ein Restaurant, das $4 für Zutaten ausgibt und eine 70%-Lebensmittelkostenspanne anstrebt, landet bei etwa $13.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: Es ist einfach und sicher, und es hat einen blinden Fleck: deine Kosten sind nicht die Angelegenheit des Kunden.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: Wenn niemand das Gericht bei $13 möchte, kümmert sich die Mathematik nicht darum.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **Wettbewerbsbasierte Preisgestaltung.** Schau, was alle anderen berechnen, und positioniere dich dagegen — Anpassung, leicht darunter oder bewusst darüber.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: Tankstellen tun dies in nahezu Echtzeit.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: Das Risiko besteht darin, dass du deine Strategie an deine Rivalen auslagert, und wenn sie falsch liegen, tust du es auch.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **Wertbasierte Preisgestaltung.** Beginne am anderen Ende: Was ist das für den Käufer wert?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: Ein Paar $200 Brillen mit Stärke und ein Paar $600 können fast gleich viel zu produzieren kosten.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: Der Unterschied ist das, was der Käufer über die Fassung glaubt.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Dies ist die Methode, zu der die meisten Vermarkter drängen, weil sie beim Kunden beginnt, nicht bei der Kalkulationstabelle.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: Dann gibt es die zweite Ebene: **psychologische Preisgestaltung** — wie die Zahl *gelesen* wird, nicht nur was sie ist.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *Charm-Preisgestaltung*: $9.99 statt $10. Die Forschung zeigt im Allgemeinen einen kleinen, aber echten Nachfrageauftrieb, hauptsächlich weil wir von links nach rechts lesen und uns an der "9" verankern. Der Effekt ist bescheiden und funktioniert am besten bei wertegesteuerten, alltäglichen Einkäufen.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *Prestige-Preisgestaltung*: eine glatte $500 statt $499. Bei Luxusgütern signalisiert eine ganze Zahl Vertrauen; das Rabattsignal würde das Produkt unterwerten.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *Verankerung*: ein $1,200 Laptop neben einem $799 angezeigt zu machen, lässt die $799 angemessen wirken. Die erste Zahl, die du siehst, setzt den mentalen Maßstab.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *Köder-Effekt*: kleine Popcorn $4, große $8 fühlt sich wie zu viel an — bis ein Medium bei $7.50 erscheint und die große plötzlich wie ein Schnäppchen aussieht. Das Medium ist nicht da zum Verkaufen; es ist da, um die große gut aussehen zu lassen.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: Die dritte Ebene: **Preisdiskriminierung** — unterschiedliche Käufer unterschiedliche Preise für im Wesentlichen dieselbe Sache berechnen.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Es klingt fragwürdig, und der Name hilft nicht, aber es ist normalerweise legal und macht oft alle besser dran.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Ökonomen ordnen es in drei Grade ein:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *Erstes Grad*: ein maßgeschneiderter Preis pro Kunde. Selten im Einzelhandel, häufig bei Autohäusern und B2B-Verträgen.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *Zweites Grad*: der Preis hängt davon ab, **was du wählst** — Größe, Stufe oder Menge. Costco Großpackungen, Spotify Free vs. Premium, die 12/16/20 oz Tassen eines Kaffeehauses. Kunden sortieren sich selbst.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *Drittes Grad*: der Preis hängt davon ab, **wer du bist** — Student, Senior oder Militärrabatte; regionale Preisgestaltung.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: Die verbindende Idee: verschiedene Menschen sind bereit, unterschiedliche Beträge zu zahlen, und ein einziger Preis lässt entweder Geld liegen oder schließt Kunden aus.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: Preisdiskriminierung ermöglicht es einem Verkäufer, von beiden Enden mehr zu verdienen.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Eine wichtige rechtliche Anmerkung: unterschiedliche Preise an verschiedene *Verbraucher* zu berechnen, ist in den USA generell legal.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: Der Robinson-Patman Act beschränkt die Preisdiskriminierung zwischen *konkurrierenden Geschäftskäufern* derselben Waren, und Kartellgesetze verbieten *Preisabsprachen* — Wettbewerber, die sich auf Preise einigen.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: Das sind andere Dinge als ein Seniorenrabatt.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: Buche einen Flug von Chicago O'Hare nach Denver und du wirst alle drei Schichten auf einem Bildschirm sehen.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: Die Fluggesellschaft setzt keine Preise nach Kosten fest.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: Sobald das Flugzeug fliegt, betragen die Grenzkosten für einen weiteren Passagier ungefähr den Treibstoff für sein Körpergewicht und eine Dose Soda — sagen wir $30.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: Doch die Tarife reichen von $89 bis $450 auf demselben Flugzeug am selben Dienstag.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: Das ist **wertbasierte Preisgestaltung**, die auf **Preisdiskriminierung** trifft.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: Wer zahlt $450?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: Der Berater, der Montag früh bucht, Donnerstag abend zurückkehrt und acht Tage voraus gebucht hat.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: Wer zahlt $89?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: Der Reisende, der sieben Wochen im Voraus gebucht hat, Dienstag bis Samstag fliegt und einen Mittelsitz hinten nicht stört.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: Die Fluggesellschaft fragt niemals "bist du ein Geschäftsreisender?"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — es muss nicht.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: Es schafft Hürden: Kaufvorlaufanforderungen, Samstagabend-Aufenthalte, Änderungsgebühren.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: Geschäftsreisende werden diese Hürden nicht überwinden, daher sortieren sie sich selbst in den teuren Tarif.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: Das ist klassische Preisdiskriminierung zweiten Grades.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: Schau dir jetzt die Sitzverteilung an.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: Basic Economy bei $89, Main Cabin bei $129, Comfort+ bei $189.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: Die meisten Reisenden wählen nicht Basic — es erlaubt kein Handgepäck oder Sitzplatzwahl.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: Es existiert vor allem, um die $129 wie die vernünftige Mitte wirken zu lassen.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **Köder-Effekt** in der Praxis.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: Und der Tarif zeigt $129, nicht $130.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **Charm-Preisgestaltung** macht ihre kleine stille Arbeit.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: Vergleiche das mit einem Delta One transkontinentalen Sitz zum Preis von $1,200 — eine glatte runde Zahl.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: Niemand, der vierstellig für einen liegenden Sitz ausgibt, möchte $1,199 sehen.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **Prestige-Preisgestaltung** übernimmt, wo Charm-Preisgestaltung aufhört zu funktionieren.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3-Punkte-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. Preise werden auf drei Wegen festgelegt — aus Kosten, von Wettbewerbern oder vom Kundenwert — und wertbasierte Preisgestaltung ist normalerweise am profitabelsten, weil sie beim Käufer beginnt, nicht bei der Kalkulationstabelle.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. Psychologische Preisgestaltung prägt, wie eine Zahl gelesen wird: $9.99 für alltäglichen Wert, eine glatte $500 für Luxus, und Köder oder Anker, um die Zieloption angemessen aussehen zu lassen.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. Preisdiskriminierung berechnet verschiedenen Käufern unterschiedliche Beträge für fast dasselbe Produkt, unter Verwendung von Selbstwahlmethoden (Stufen, Größen, Vorauskauf) oder Identität (Student, Senior) — und genau so trägt ein Flugzeug gleichzeitig $89 und $450 Passagiere.

vi.title: [Marketing 101 #8] Tại Sao Cà phê $4.99 của Bạn Thực ra Không Phải Là Về Cà phê

segments.src: > Price is the only part of marketing that brings money in — everything else spends it. This lesson covers how prices get set, why $9.99 feels cheaper than $10, and how the same seat on the same flight can cost three different amounts.
segments.tr: > Giá là phần duy nhất của tiếp thị mang lại doanh thu — mọi thứ khác đều tiêu tốn tiền. Bài học này đề cập đến cách xác định giá, tại sao $9.99 cảm thấy rẻ hơn $10, và cách cùng một chỗ ngồi trên cùng một chuyến bay có thể có ba mức giá khác nhau.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Most people think pricing is arithmetic: add up your costs, tack on a profit, done.
segments.tr: Hầu hết mọi người nghĩ rằng định giá là số học: cộng chi phí của bạn, thêm lợi nhuận, xong.

segments.src: That's one real method, but it's the least interesting one.
segments.tr: Đó là một phương pháp thực sự, nhưng nó là phương pháp ít thú vị nhất.

segments.src: There are three broad ways companies land on a number.
segments.tr: Có ba cách chung thương mại đưa ra một con số.

segments.src: **Cost-based pricing.** Start with what it costs you to make the thing, add a markup.
segments.tr: **Định giá theo chi phí.** Bắt đầu với chi phí sản xuất, thêm biên lợi nhuận.

segments.src: A restaurant that spends $4 on ingredients and wants a 70% food-cost margin lands near $13.
segments.tr: Một nhà hàng chi $4 cho nguyên liệu và muốn biên độ chi phí thực phẩm 70% sẽ định giá gần $13.

segments.src: It's simple and safe, and it has a blind spot: your costs are none of the customer's business.
segments.tr: Nó đơn giản và an toàn, nhưng có một điểm mù: chi phí của bạn không liên quan gì đến khách hàng.

segments.src: If nobody wants the dish at $13, the math doesn't care.
segments.tr: Nếu không ai muốn món ăn này ở mức $13, phép toán không quan tâm.

segments.src: **Competition-based pricing.** Look at what everyone else charges and position yourself against it — matching, slightly under, or deliberately above.
segments.tr: **Định giá theo cạnh tranh.** Xem những gì người khác tính phí và định vị bản thân so với nó — khớp, thấp hơn một chút, hoặc cao hơn cố ý.

segments.src: Gas stations do this in near-real time.
segments.tr: Các trạm xăng dầu làm điều này gần như trong thời gian thực.

segments.src: The risk is that you outsource your strategy to your rivals, and if they're wrong, so are you.
segments.tr: Nguy hiểm là bạn giao chiến lược cho đối thủ, và nếu họ sai, bạn cũng sai.

segments.src: **Value-based pricing.** Start at the other end: what is this worth to the buyer?
segments.tr: **Định giá theo giá trị.** Bắt đầu từ đầu kia: điều này có giá trị gì với người mua?

segments.src: A $200 pair of prescription glasses and a $600 pair may cost nearly the same to produce.
segments.tr: Một đôi kính respec $200 và một đôi $600 có thể có chi phí sản xuất gần như nhau.

segments.src: The gap is what the buyer believes about the frame.
segments.tr: Khoảng cách là những gì người mua tin về khung.

segments.src: This is the method most marketers push toward, because it starts with the customer instead of the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Đây là phương pháp mà hầu hết các nhà tiếp thị đẩy, vì nó bắt đầu với khách hàng thay vì bảng tính.

segments.src: Then there's the second layer: **psychological pricing** — how the number *reads*, not just what it is.
segments.tr: Sau đó là lớp thứ hai: **định giá tâm lý** — cách con số *đọc*, không chỉ những gì nó là.

segments.src: - *Charm pricing*: $9.99 instead of $10. Research generally shows a small but real lift in demand, mostly because we read left to right and anchor on the "9." The effect is modest and works best on value-driven, everyday purchases.
segments.tr: - *Định giá quyến rũ*: $9.99 thay vì $10. Nghiên cứu thường cho thấy sự tăng nhỏ nhưng thực sự về nhu cầu, chủ yếu vì chúng ta đọc từ trái sang phải và neo vào "9." Hiệu ứng là khiêm tốn và hoạt động tốt nhất đối với các mua hàng hàng ngày được thúc đẩy bởi giá trị.

segments.src: - *Prestige pricing*: a round $500 rather than $499. For luxury goods, a clean number signals confidence; the discount cue would undercut the product.
segments.tr: - *Định giá danh tiếng*: một $500 tròn thay vì $499. Đối với hàng xa xỉ, một con số sạch sẽ hiển thị sự tự tin; tín hiệu chiết khấu sẽ phá hủy sản phẩm.

segments.src: - *Anchoring*: showing a $1,200 laptop next to a $799 one makes the $799 feel reasonable. The first number you see sets the mental yardstick.
segments.tr: - *Neo*: hiển thị một laptop $1,200 cạnh một cái $799 làm cho $799 cảm thấy hợp lý. Con số đầu tiên bạn thấy đặt thước đo tinh thần.

segments.src: - *Decoy effect*: small popcorn $4, large $8 feels like a stretch — until a medium appears at $7.50 and the large suddenly looks like a bargain. The medium isn't there to sell; it's there to make the large look good.
segments.tr: - *Hiệu ứng mồi nhử*: bỏng ngô nhỏ $4, to $8 cảm thấy như một khoảng cách — cho đến khi một cái vừa xuất hiện ở $7.50 và cái to đột nhiên trông như một khoá. Cái vừa không ở đó để bán; nó ở đó để làm cho cái to trông tốt.

segments.src: The third layer: **price discrimination** — charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same thing.
segments.tr: Lớp thứ ba: **phân biệt giá** — tính phí khác nhau cho những người mua khác nhau cho cơ bản cùng một điều.

segments.src: It sounds shady, and the name doesn't help, but it's usually legal and often makes everyone better off.
segments.tr: Nó nghe có vẻ đáng ngờ, và cái tên không giúp gì, nhưng nó thường hợp pháp và thường làm cho mọi người tốt hơn.

segments.src: Economists sort it into three degrees:
segments.tr: Các nhà kinh tế sắp xếp nó thành ba độ:

segments.src: - *First degree*: a custom price per customer. Rare in retail, common in car dealerships and B2B contracts.
segments.tr: - *Mức độ thứ nhất*: một giá tùy chỉnh cho mỗi khách hàng. Hiếm trong bán lẻ, phổ biến trong các đại lý ô tô và hợp đồng B2B.

segments.src: - *Second degree*: the price depends on **what you choose** — size, tier, or quantity. Costco bulk packs, Spotify Free vs. Premium, a coffee shop's 12/16/20 oz cups. Customers sort themselves.
segments.tr: - *Mức độ thứ hai*: giá phụ thuộc vào **những gì bạn chọn** — kích thước, cấp độ hoặc số lượng. Các gói hàng loạt Costco, Spotify miễn phí so với Premium, cốc 12/16/20 oz của một quán cà phê. Khách hàng tự sắp xếp.

segments.src: - *Third degree*: the price depends on **who you are** — student, senior, or military discounts; regional pricing.
segments.tr: - *Mức độ thứ ba*: giá phụ thuộc vào **bạn là ai** — học sinh, cao tuổi hoặc chiết khấu quân sự; định giá khu vực.

segments.src: The unifying idea: different people are willing to pay different amounts, and a single price either leaves money on the table or leaves customers behind.
segments.tr: Ý tưởng thống nhất: những người khác nhau sẵn sàng trả các khoản tiền khác nhau, và một giá duy nhất hoặc để tiền trên bàn hoặc để lại khách hàng.

segments.src: Price discrimination lets a seller capture more of both ends.
segments.tr: Phân biệt giá cho phép người bán nắm bắt nhiều hơn ở cả hai đầu.

segments.src: One legal note worth knowing: charging different prices to different *consumers* is generally fine in the U.S.
segments.tr: Một ghi chú pháp lý đáng biết: tính phí khác nhau cho các *người tiêu dùng* khác nhau thường ổn trong U.S.

segments.src: The Robinson-Patman Act restricts price discrimination between *competing business buyers* of the same commodity, and antitrust law prohibits *price fixing* — competitors agreeing on prices.
segments.tr: Luật Robinson-Patman hạn chế phân biệt giá giữa *các nhà mua kinh doanh cạnh tranh* của cùng một hàng hóa, và luật chống độc quyền cấm *định giá* — các đối thủ thỏa thuận về giá.

segments.src: Those are different things from a senior discount.
segments.tr: Những điều đó khác với chiết khấu cho người cao tuổi.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Book a flight from Chicago O'Hare to Denver and you'll see all three layers in one screen.
segments.tr: Đặt chuyến bay từ Chicago O'Hare đến Denver và bạn sẽ thấy cả ba lớp trong một màn hình.

segments.src: The airline doesn't price by cost.
segments.tr: Hãng hàng không không định giá theo chi phí.

segments.src: Once the plane is flying, the marginal cost of one more passenger is roughly the fuel for their body weight and a can of soda — call it $30.
segments.tr: Một khi máy bay đang bay, chi phí biên tế của thêm một hành khách là khoảng nhiên liệu cho trọng lượng cơ thể của họ và một lon soda — gọi nó là $30.

segments.src: Yet fares range from $89 to $450 on the same aircraft on the same Tuesday.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, giá vé dao động từ $89 đến $450 trên cùng một máy bay vào cùng một ngày thứ ba.

segments.src: That's **value-based pricing** meeting **price discrimination**.
segments.tr: Đó là **định giá theo giá trị** gặp **phân biệt giá**.

segments.src: Who's paying $450?
segments.tr: Ai đang trả $450?

segments.src: The consultant booking Monday morning, returning Thursday night, who booked eight days out.
segments.tr: Cố vấn đặt sáng thứ hai, trở về tối thứ năm, người đã đặt chỗ tám ngày trước.

segments.src: Who's paying $89?
segments.tr: Ai đang trả $89?

segments.src: The traveler who booked seven weeks ahead, flies Tuesday to Saturday, and doesn't mind a middle seat in the back.
segments.tr: Người du lịch đã đặt chỗ bảy tuần trước, bay từ thứ ba đến thứ bảy, và không phiền ghế giữa phía sau.

segments.src: The airline never asks "are you a business traveler?"
segments.tr: Hãng hàng không không bao giờ hỏi "bạn có phải là một du khách kinh doanh?"

segments.src: — it doesn't have to.
segments.tr: — nó không cần phải.

segments.src: It builds fences: advance-purchase requirements, Saturday-night stays, change fees.
segments.tr: Nó xây dựng hàng rào: yêu cầu mua trước, ở lại đêm thứ bảy, phí thay đổi.

segments.src: Business travelers won't jump those fences, so they sort themselves into the expensive fare.
segments.tr: Những du khách kinh doanh sẽ không nhảy qua những hàng rào đó, vì vậy họ tự sắp xếp thành giá vé đắt tiền.

segments.src: That's textbook second-degree discrimination.
segments.tr: Đó là sách giáo khoa phân biệt mức độ thứ hai.

segments.src: Now look at the seat map.
segments.tr: Bây giờ hãy nhìn vào bản đồ ghế.

segments.src: Basic Economy at $89, Main Cabin at $129, Comfort+ at $189.
segments.tr: Basic Economy ở $89, Main Cabin ở $129, Comfort+ ở $189.

segments.src: Most travelers don't pick Basic — it doesn't allow a carry-on or seat selection.
segments.tr: Hầu hết du khách không chọn Basic — nó không cho phép hành lý ký gửi hoặc chọn chỗ.

segments.src: It exists largely to make $129 feel like the sensible middle.
segments.tr: Nó tồn tại chủ yếu để làm cho $129 cảm thấy như trung bình hợp lý.

segments.src: **Decoy effect**, in the wild.
segments.tr: **Hiệu ứng mồi nhử**, trong tự nhiên.

segments.src: And the fare reads $129, not $130.
segments.tr: Và giá vé đọc $129, không phải $130.

segments.src: **Charm pricing**, doing its small quiet work.
segments.tr: **Định giá quyến rũ**, làm công việc yên tĩnh nhỏ của nó.

segments.src: Compare that to a Delta One transcontinental seat listed at $1,200 — a clean round number.
segments.tr: So sánh điều đó với ghế liên lục địa Delta One được niêm yết ở $1,200 — một con số tròn sạch sẽ.

segments.src: Nobody spending four figures on a lie-flat seat wants to see $1,199.
segments.tr: Không ai chi bốn chữ số cho ghế nằm phẳng muốn thấy $1,199.

segments.src: **Prestige pricing** takes over where charm pricing stops working.
segments.tr: **Định giá danh tiếng** tiếp quản nơi định giá quyến rũ dừng hoạt động.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt 3 Dòng

segments.src: 1. Prices are set three ways — from costs, from competitors, or from customer value — and value-based pricing is usually the most profitable because it starts with the buyer, not the spreadsheet.
segments.tr: 1. Giá được xác định theo ba cách — từ chi phí, từ các đối thủ, hoặc từ giá trị khách hàng — và định giá theo giá trị thường là lợi nhuận cao nhất vì nó bắt đầu với người mua, không phải bảng tính.

segments.src: 2. Psychological pricing shapes how a number is read: $9.99 for everyday value, a round $500 for luxury, and decoys or anchors to make the target option look reasonable.
segments.tr: 2. Định giá tâm lý định hình cách đọc một con số: $9.99 cho giá trị hàng ngày, $500 tròn cho xa xỉ, và mồi nhử hoặc neo để làm cho lựa chọn đích trông hợp lý.

segments.src: 3. Price discrimination charges different buyers different amounts for nearly the same product, using self-selection (tiers, sizes, advance purchase) or identity (student, senior) — and it's how one plane carries $89 and $450 passengers at once.
segments.tr: 3. Phân biệt giá tính phí các khoản tiền khác nhau cho những người mua khác nhau cho gần như cùng một sản phẩm, sử dụng tự chọn (các cấp, kích thước, mua trước) hoặc danh tính (học sinh, cao tuổi) — và đó là cách một chiếc máy bay chở hành khách $89 và $450 cùng một lúc.

segments.src: The medium size sells poorly, but the theater keeps it on the menu anyway.

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật Ngữ Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Cost-based pricing** — Setting a price by starting from production cost and adding a markup or target margin.
segments.tr: - **Định giá theo chi phí** — Đặt giá bằng cách bắt đầu từ chi phí sản xuất và thêm biên lợi nhuận hoặc biên lợi nhuận mục tiêu.

segments.src: - **Value-based pricing** — Setting a price from what the product is worth to the customer, independent of what it cost to make.
segments.tr: - **Định giá theo giá trị** — Đặt giá từ những gì sản phẩm có giá trị cho khách hàng, độc lập với chi phí sản xuất.

segments.src: - **Charm pricing** — Ending a price just below a round number (e.g., $9.99) so it reads as meaningfully cheaper.
segments.tr: - **Định giá quyến rũ** — Kết thúc giá chỉ dưới một con số tròn (ví dụ: $9.99) để nó đọc rẻ hơn một cách có ý nghĩa.

segments.src: - **Anchoring** — The tendency to judge a price against the first number encountered, which becomes a mental reference point.
segments.tr: - **Neo** — Xu hướng đánh giá giá so với con số đầu tiên gặp phải, trở thành điểm tham chiếu tinh thần.

segments.src: - **Price discrimination** — Charging different buyers different prices for essentially the same product, based on what they choose (second degree) or who they are (third degree).
segments.tr: - **Phân biệt giá** — Tính phí khác nhau cho những người mua khác nhau cho cơ bản cùng một sản phẩm, dựa trên những gì họ chọn (mức độ thứ hai) hoặc họ là ai (mức độ thứ ba).
*Đáp án: 1 → C.

segments.src: The owner ignores the $80 cost and prices from perceived customer worth — that's value-based pricing.
segments.tr: Chủ sở hữu bỏ qua chi phí $80 và định giá từ giá trị khách hàng được cảm nhận — đó là định giá theo giá trị.

segments.src: A poorly selling middle option that makes the adjacent premium option look like a bargain is a decoy; the $0.50 gap between Medium and Large makes the Large nearly irresistible.
segments.tr: Một lựa chọn trung bình bán chạy kém làm cho lựa chọn cao cấp liền kề trông như một khoá là một mồi nhử; khoảng cách $0.50 giữa Medium và Large làm cho Large gần như không thể cưỡng lại.

segments.src: Third-degree price discrimination sets prices by observable customer group — age, student status, region — which is exactly what a senior discount does.
segments.tr: Phân biệt giá mức độ thứ ba đặt giá theo nhóm khách hàng có thể quan sát được — tuổi, tình trạng học sinh, vùng — chính xác là những gì chiết khấu cao tuổi làm.
